concept.name: Weekly pivot
concept.definition: A pivot point computed from the previous calendar week's high, low, and close, applied to the current week. On StockCharts' convention, pivots for 30- to 120-minute charts use the prior week's data and remain fixed for the entire week.
concept.intuition: Last week's price action condenses into this week's bias line and outer reference levels.
concept.mechanics: Computed at the week's start as P = (prior week H + L + C)/3 with derived S/R levels; fixed for the week and recalculated on the first trading day of the next week.
concept.formula: P = (H_prev_week + L_prev_week + C_prev_week)/3; S1 = 2P - H; R1 = 2P - L; S2 = P - (H - L); R2 = P + (H - L).
concept.failure_modes: Same structural limits as all pivots: strong weekly trends can leave the pivot behind on day one, and holiday-shortened weeks distort the inputs.
concept.misconceptions: That weekly pivots are more 'reliable' than daily ones by nature; they are merely slower-moving references with the same heuristic status.
concept.example: Last week a stock printed H 110, L 100, C 108: this week's weekly pivot is P = 106, with R1 = 112 and S1 = 102 on the 60-minute chart.
